long_biography.plain_text:
Namik Tanik built part of his concrete-pipe business by buying a German plant and making the machinery he could not afford to purchase. His engineering partner, Kerim Kavacıklı, supplied the technical expertise; their operation subsequently exported components to Germany. Tanik brought his companies together as NATA Holding in 1995.

NATA's expansion into Turkmenistan began with the acquisition of shares in Net Yapı, a contractor struggling to complete its projects there. Tanik's team finished those commitments and went on to undertake larger infrastructure schemes. The group's projects included Bereket train station, road bridges and railway signalling works in Turkmenistan.
